subject: Parse Labs hosted API traffic & pricing check-in
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@parse.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Parse Labs hosted API traffic & pricing check-in

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick recap and a couple of asks so we can get the MAP and pricing proposal over to your procurement team.

Recap (what we heard)
- Baseline expected monthly tokens: 180,000,000 - 250,000,000 (you mentioned ~200M as the conservative baseline; marketing pushes could lift to ~250M).
- Average tokens per request: ~350 tokens (chat-style truncation + metadata).
- Peak concurrency: short bursts up to ~220 TPS (10–15 minute promotion windows).
- 99th percentile sustained window during business hours: ~70–80 TPS for ~2–3 hour periods.
- Budget target (internal): $18–$26 per 1M tokens for hosted pricing; procurement asked for clear $/1M bands and a committed option.

Asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm the 200M baseline and the 220 TPS burst ceiling (we'll use these for SLA and autoscaling sizing)?
2) Does the procurement team have a preferred cadence for billing (monthly vs quarterly) and any PO/WO numbering constraints?
3) I'll attach a draft MAP and a quick cost sketch — review and flag anything off before we do an initial commercial.

Attachments:
- mutual_action_plan.xlsx (draft timeline + decision owners)

If that matches, I’ll follow up with two pricing bands (committed vs on-demand hosted) and a short note on how we handle peak TPS (burst vs queueing behavior).

Thanks,
Monica

Monica — thanks for the clear recap. Quick confirmations from our side: 
- Baseline we can commit to in Q4 is 200M tokens / month (with marketing spikes likely up to 250M in one-off months).
- Average tokens per call ~350 is accurate.
- Peak TPS: we have observed 220 TPS in short promo spikes; typical 99th is indeed ~75 TPS.
- Procurement prefers monthly billing but is flexible if a quarterly arrangement simplifies invoicing.

I'll loop in purchasing if you need a draft PO template; for now, please include the $/1M bands and a committed-tier example — procurement will want a clear committed discount over on-demand.

—Alyssa
Director of Product 
Parse Labs
alyssa@parse.ai
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@parse.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Parse Labs hosted API traffic & pricing check-in

Thanks Alyssa — that helps. Attaching a short cost sketch (redwood_cost_estimates_sep14.pdf) and the updated MAP. Below are two starting commercial constructions for you and procurement to review; these are examples — we can adjust bands and committed volumes.

Option A — 12mo committed hosted (recommended for predictability)
- Commitment: 200M tokens / month minimum
- Price: $19 / 1M tokens up to commit (applies to 200M baseline)
- Overages (on top of commit): $22 / 1M tokens
- Benefit: Guaranteed compute capacity, lower unit price, priority routing during regional capacity pressure

Option B — On-demand hosted (no commit)
- Price tiers: $26 / 1M tokens for monthly usage <= 250M; $23 / 1M tokens for monthly usage > 250M (automated tiering)
- No minimum commitment; standard shared capacity SLA

Peak TPS handling and SLA note
- We saw you call out 220 TPS bursts. For hosted customers this is handled via burst capacity with automated routing and soft-fallback to compatible model variants. We recommend a short warm-up window for large promotive bursts (15–30 minutes) to ensure autoscaling reaches the higher concurrency level.
- If >220 TPS sustained for >30 minutes becomes common, we typically recommend Dedicated capacity or a committed throughput add-on (we can include a proposal).

Open questions I flagged for procurement
- Target $/1M indicated as $18–$26 — our proposed committed band centers at $19 (close to your lower bound). Is there flexibility to trade off term (18 vs 12 months) or commit size for a lower $/1M?
- Will procurement require SOC2 or additional evidence bundles upfront (we can attach SOC2 + network diagrams)?

Next steps
1) If numbers look good, I’ll prepare a redline-friendly commercial term sheet and a PO template for your purchasing team.
2) Proposed quick sync w/ procurement next week (30 min).

Attachments:
- redwood_cost_estimates_sep14.pdf (two-band math + example invoice)
- mutual_action_plan.xlsx (updated with commit option)

Best,
Monica
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

If Parse anticipates multiple overlapping promo windows, let’s talk Dedicated sizing (we’ll run a short simulation).

Monica — I’ll prep a one-pager (technical brief) on burst handling and include it in the MAP before the procurement sync. Alyssa — are you available Tues 9/21 for a 30-minute procurement + infra sync?

Thanks,
